tasks.title: Design PostgreSQL schema for users and tasks (id, user_id, title, description, completed, created_at) with indexes on user_id and completed, plus migration scripts
Scaffold Node/Express REST API and React app, with environment config, HTTPS setup, and user-scoped auth middleware so users only access their own tasks
Prepare design tokens (colors, Inter typography, spacing) and shared UI components: buttons, inputs, task card, checkbox, filter chips, status badge, modal, toast
Build Create Task API (POST /tasks) with title validation (required, max 100 chars) and optional description
Build New Task screen: title and description inputs, character counter, inline validation error, Save/Cancel, success toast
Build View Task List API (GET /tasks with status filter all/active/completed) and Task Details endpoint (GET /tasks/:id)
Build Task List screen: header with open count, filter tabs, task cards, status badges, floating add button, and Empty State variants
Build Complete Task API (PATCH /tasks/:id status toggle) and UI: list checkbox with optimistic update, Task Details toggle button, undo toast
Build Task Details screen with summary card, description block, created date, and navigation from list
Build Delete Task API (DELETE /tasks/:id) and Delete Confirmation dialog with Delete/Keep Task actions, list collapse animation, and toast
Apply accessibility and responsive polish: focus rings, aria-live errors, 44px touch targets, keyboard support, 720px centered layout on desktop, empty state illustration
End-to-end testing of all acceptance criteria, basic load test at 100 concurrent users (<2s list load), and HTTPS deployment with uptime monitoring

risks: Authentication and per-user data isolation are required by security NFRs but no auth feature is specified, so scope creep or delay is possible; use a minimal token-based login or seeded user for MVP.
Database schema was not provided in requirements, so late schema changes could force rework of API and UI.
Task Details screen, undo toast, and character counter appear in the design but not in the acceptance criteria, risking over-building; keep them minimal.
Meeting the 99.5% uptime and 100-concurrent-user performance targets may need hosting, connection pooling, and monitoring work beyond the MVP timeline.
Delete is permanent while the undo toast applies only to status changes, so confirmation flow bugs could cause accidental data loss; cover with tests.
